checks: Re-derived L_vib from the 3-2 limit: alpha<0.05 x I_HCN 1.25 Jy/beam km/s, with L'=3.25e7 S nu^-2 D_L^2 (1+z)^-3 and D~44 Mpc, gives ~33 Lsun vs the worker's 29 Lsun. This is the same order, and a ~10% distance/convention difference does not matter against a >=60x margin to the CON threshold.

Read s42 (limit method): the template is the HCN v=0 profile, the HCO+ wing is a nuisance fitted with 4 models, the noise comes from line-free channels, and the limit is a profile-likelihood 3 sigma. The N limits are stable across wing models (0.025-0.05), so it is a serious attempt that models the HCO+ blend. The 1e partner at +38 km/s lies on HCN v=0, and alpha<0.05 also bounds its contamination of the HCN/HCO+ ratio.

Falstad table: Sigma recomputed from L_vib and size for N (65/(pi/4*347*250)=0.0010) and the T_b values reproduce. I checked the CON/non-CON flags against the Sigma>1 criterion and they are consistent (ESO173, ArpII E and F12112 are detected but have Sigma<1, so non-CON). Our 0.24 arcsec peak T_b 0.18 K corresponds to ~0.5 mJy/beam, consistent with 17.6 mJy spread over ~40 beams.

Nishimura split: the groups are as stated (n=3 CON, 2 vib-detected non-CON, 11-12 non-detected, 6 unclassified), the tests are honestly reported as not significant (p=0.09-0.23), and the NGC5734 limit handling is disclosed. I agree with the conclusion: N is not CON-like and its ratio matches the non-detected median. The report.json entries are valid (confidence values high/medium/low, 234 results). No conflict with the forum (p0055, p0056, Q6 dust bound).
notes_for_questioner: Caveats the editor should carry into the post: (1) the vib limit assumes the vib profile equals the HCN v=0 profile and excludes CON-level luminous vib emission, not moderate pumping (Tvib 150-300 K, alpha<0.04). (2) Band 7 860 um continuum was not done separately; the 1.1 mm T_b is sufficient. (3) n=3 CONs, so no claim of a CON ratio enhancement. Open: with IR pumping excluded at the CON level, remaining discriminators for the N core HCN excess are opacity (H13CN limits), abundance, and a collisional-excitation/temperature difference, so prioritise the H13CN/H13CO+ and RADEX two-zone items. Also quantify the 1e contamination (alpha<0.05) as a systematic on the N HCN/HCO+ ratio (<=5%).
